Imagine securing an 8% interest rate on your investment in one of Alabama’s most promising counties. This opportunity awaits you at the Tax Sale in Lee County, where investing can lead to significant returns.

The Tax Sale in Lee County is an event you shouldn’t miss. When owners fail to pay their taxes, the county conducts a Land Sale to recoup back taxes. This sale is scheduled for the first Wednesday in May each year at the Lee County Courthouse on South 9th Street in Opelika. This is a live, in-person auction.

Understanding Tax Lien Certificates

Here’s what you need to know to get involved:

  1. Auction Process:

    Properties are sold to the highest bidder. Winners receive a Certificate which has up to a 3-year redemption period. If the land is redeemed, you will receive your investment back plus a solid 8% interest per year.
  2. Registration:

    Interested investors should check the county’s website for registration details. They clearly outlined registration steps and required documentation.

Economic Highlights and Community Appeal

  • Economic Overview:

    The economy of Lee County, AL, employs about 79.4k people. The largest industries are Educational Services, Health Care & Social Assistance, and Manufacturing. The highest-paying industries include Finance & Insurance and Public Administration​​.
  • Community:

    Lee County offers a mix of urban and rural lifestyles with ample opportunities for outdoor recreation, cultural events, and educational growth. It’s a vibrant community with a supportive infrastructure for businesses and investors.

Pro Tips for Investors

  1. Research Local Laws: Ensure you understand the legal framework and key regulations in Lee County before participating.
  2. Visit the County Website: Regularly check for updates on auction dates and registration requirements.
  3. Contact the County Office: If you have any questions, reach out to the Lee County Revenue Commissioner’s office for assistance.

FAQs

Q: What happens if the property owner redeems the lien?

A: If the property owner redeems the lien, you will receive your initial investment back plus an 8% interest rate per year.

Q: How long is the redemption period?

A: The redemption period is up to 3 years.

Q: Where can I find more information?

A: Visit the Lee County Revenue Commissioner’s website for detailed information on tax sales and registration.

Investing in tax liens in Lee County can be a profitable venture if done correctly. Make sure to stay informed and prepared to make the most of this opportunity.
